title: fix(clone.say): a labelled top rule reads as no rule, so an empty box reads dirty
description:
## symptom

`rhx clone say @:<slug>` withholds every say with `input-region-dirty` while the target clone's
real input row is empty (`❯` alone). seen twice in a row on 2026-11-05 (rhachet 1.51.0), target a
claude session mid-turn, in auto mode.

## cause, at the line

`dist/domain.operations/clone/screen/computeCloneInputState.js:43-46`

```js
const isRuleRow = (line) => {
    const trimmed = line.trim();
    return /^─+$/.test(trimmed) && trimmed.length >= 20;
};
```

claude draws the box's TOP rule with the session label inside it:

```
────────────────────────────────── mechanic ─
❯
─────────────────────────────────────────────
```

the labelled row fails `^─+$`, so `getInputBand` (same file, :216) picks the LAST two rule rows =
an earlier rule far up the screen + the box's bottom rule. the band then holds ~25 rows of the
brain's own bright tool output, `contentBright` is non-empty, and `region` reads `dirty` (:330).

## the worse form — `focus-unrecognized`, never force-able

once the earlier plain rule scrolls off the viewport, only ONE row passes `isRuleRow` (the box's
bottom rule). `getInputBand` returns null at `ruleRows.length < 2`, so the verdict becomes
`focus-unrecognized`, which `--force` cannot override, and whose hint says to tear the clone
down and re-enroll — a destructive remedy for a healthy clone whose box sits plainly at the foot
(`── mechanic ─` / `❯` / `────`). measured 2026-11-07 on the same clone.

## evidence

`clone get --what buffer` returned a 27-row "input box" that ends at the `── mechanic ─` row and
holds the brain's tool output, not human text. the debug log's screen shows the true box at the
foot: labelled rule, empty `❯`, plain rule.

## fix

accept a rule row that carries an embedded label: a row whose trimmed form is `─` runs plus at
most one short label, e.g. `/^─{3,}(\s+\S.{0,40}\S\s+─+)?$/` with the length floor kept. the
bottom rule stays the plain form.

## clamp

a unit case for `computeCloneInputState` over a captured screen with a labelled top rule, an
empty `❯`, and bright tool output above it: expect `input: 'clear'`. red on 1.51.0, green with
the fix. a second case with typed text after `❯` must still read `dirty`, so the gate still
refuses what it must.

## false hint

the refusal says "a human mid-type"; here no human typed. the hint sends a caller to `--force`,
which is safe only when the true box is empty — a caller cannot tell that from the message.
